1.explanation: Highlight.js’s JavaScript/ES6 grammar is defined in these two files. src/languages/lib/ecmascript.js contains the core ES6 class syntax modes, and src/languages/javascript.js ties that into the JavaScript language definition used by highlightAuto. Since method definitions inside class bodies aren’t matched by the existing regex/mode in ecmascript.js, they never get the “function” scope. Updating the class-method matching patterns in ecmascript.js (and ensuring javascript.js includes them) will allow member functions to be highlighted correctly.
1.bug_scenario: When markdown containing an ES6 class is rendered and passed through highlight.js (via highlightAuto in marked), the member methods inside the class (constructor, componentDidMount, render, custom methods, etc.) are not receiving the "function" highlighting. In the screenshot you can see a React class definition where keywords like "class" and built-ins (e.g. "super") are highlighted, but the method names and parentheses are rendered as plain text.

2.explanation: The grammar rules for ES6 in highlight.js live in src/languages/lib/ecmascript.js, which defines how class bodies and their methods are parsed and tokenized. If member functions inside a class aren’t matched by its regex patterns, they will not be highlighted. The javascript.js file in src/languages augments or registers the ES6 mode for JavaScript, so any omission or override there can also prevent proper function highlighting. These files need adjustment to include a pattern matching class method definitions (name followed by parentheses) so that highlight.js will classify them as functions.
2.bug_scenario: When rendering ES6 class code blocks (e.g. class Detail extends Component { constructor(){} render(){} changeScrollTopShow(){} }) through highlight.js in React, the class member functions (constructor, render, lifecycle methods, etc.) are not being recognized or highlighted as functions. The screenshot shows the keywords (class, constructor) highlighted but method names and their parentheses are treated as plain text.
